public_rationale: Anthropic's report released on May 22, 2025 documents successful jailbreaks against Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 in its evaluation [e1]. These tests establish instruction failures but do not identify a missing world model as their cause [e1]. Anthropic's study released on March 27, 2025 links one jailbreak in Claude 3.5 Haiku partly to competing pressures from grammatical coherence and safety mechanisms [e2]. That earlier-model finding offers an alternative explanation but does not settle the claimed cause in the Claude generation available in June 2025 [e2].
limitations: The Claude 4 evaluation covers a limited attack set and does not separately measure the proposed biological or discourse representations [e1].
The mechanistic finding concerns one jailbreak in an earlier model, Claude 3.5 Haiku [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Claude cannot reliably enforce its own instructions because it cannot connect words to a world model.

statement.excerpt: Because Claude doesn’t know how to relate words on a page [such as “biological weapons”) with a model of human biology or a world model of its own conversional world (the world of discourse and user interaction) – it is at a loss to reliably enforce its own instructions.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: Claude doesn’t know how to relate words on a page
a world model of its own conversional world
at a loss to reliably enforce its own instructions
our_interpretation: The claim attributes instruction failures to a specific representational deficit. Showing that Claude can be jailbroken would establish the failure, but not its proposed cause.
The surrounding reference to the latest Claude model makes the Claude generation available in June 2025 the main subject.
Reliable enforcement means consistently following governing instructions under relevant adversarial interactions; Marcus supplies no numerical threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled studies of the relevant Claude models establish the proposed deficit and show that it materially causes instruction failures, separating it from competing explanations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled studies establish the relevant representations and show that instruction failures arise despite their effective connection to the instruction language, undermining the asserted causal explanation.

evidence.explanation: Table 2.7.A reports nonzero jailbreak success for Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, with better resistance under extended thinking. These results document susceptibility and variation in resistance, but do not identify a missing world model as the cause.

evidence.excerpt: a tension between grammatical coherence and safety mechanisms
evidence.explanation: The Claude 3.5 Haiku case study describes safety recognition competing with pressure to finish a coherent sentence. This is a material alternative explanation, but its earlier model and narrow experiment prevent a decisive conclusion about the Claude generation discussed in the post.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled studies of the Claude generation available in June 2025 that separately measure instruction compliance and the proposed biological or discourse representations. Interventions must test whether missing connections between those representations and instruction language cause failures, while distinguishing competing explanations.
